nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
The following tables set forth the major components of our noninterest expense for the periods indicated:

Noninterest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $9.8 million compared to $10.4 million for the same period in 2025, a decrease of $0.6 million, or 5.7%. Accounting, marketing, and legal fees expense was $0.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $0.2 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of $0.7 million, or 308.1%. The increase in accounting, marketing, and legal fees was primarily attributable to an increase in consulting and legal fees tied to the acquisition of Century Financial Services Corporation. Additionally, ‘Other expense’ decreased by $1.3 million, which was primarily driven by the disposition of the Company’s oil and gas assets during the second quarter of 2026.

Noninterest expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $32.0 million compared to $29.0 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of $3.0 million, or 10.4%. Salaries and employee benefits expense was $18.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $16.8 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of $1.4 million, or 8.5%.

pretax.text: Income before taxes was $13.6 million, a decrease of $0.6 million, or 4.0%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to income before taxes of $14.2 million for the same period in 2025 . Income before taxes was $40.5 million, a decrease of $2.2 million, or 5.1%, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to income before taxes of $42.6 million for the same period in 2025 .

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
We file a consolidated income tax return and recognize deferred taxes based upon the future tax consequences of temporary differences between the carrying amounts and tax basis of assets and liabilities. The process of determining the accruals for income taxes involves the exercise of considerable judgment regarding tax rates, laws, and the implementation of tax planning strategies.

For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, all of our income before income taxes was generated from domestic operations. We do not currently have exposure to foreign tax jurisdictions; as such, our jurisdictional tax mix remains concentrated within the United States and specific state jurisdictions, primarily Oklahoma.

Our provision for income taxes was $3.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3.3 million for same period in 2025. This resulted in an effective tax rate of 25.06% in 2026, compared to 23.56% in 2025. The effective tax rate differs from the U.S. federal statutory rate of 21% primarily due to the effect of state income taxes (net of federal benefit) and nondeductible expenses. The year-over-year rate change was primarily driven by the impact of Oklahoma state taxes and certain nondeductible reconciling items.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
The following tables set forth the major components of our noninterest income for the periods indicated:

Noninterest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $1.1 million compared to $2.2 million for the same period in 2025, a decrease of $1.1 million, or 51.6%. The decrease was primarily driven by a $1.2 million decline in ‘Other income and fees’, which was attributable to the absence of oil and gas related revenues during the third quarter of 2026 following the disposition of the Company’s oil and gas assets. For comparison, the Company recognized $1.3 million of oil and gas related revenues during the same period in 2025.

Noninterest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $4.0 million compared to $6.7 million for the same period in 2025, a decrease of $2.6 million, or 39.4%. The decrease was primarily driven by a $3.0 million decline in ‘Other income and fees’, which was largely attributable to a reduction in oil and gas related revenues following the disposition of the Company’s oil and gas assets early in the second quarter of 2026. The Company recognized $0.9 million of oil and gas related revenues during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $4.0 million for the same period in 2025.

intro.text: We are Bank7 Corp., a bank holding company headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. Through our wholly-owned subsidiary, Bank7, we operate twelve full-service branches in Oklahoma, Texas, and Kansas. We were formed in 2004 in connection with our acquisition of First National Bank of Medford, which was renamed Bank7 (the “Bank”). We are focused on serving business owners and entrepreneurs by delivering fast, consistent and well-designed banking solutions. As of December 31, 2025, we had total assets of $1.96 billion, total loans of $1.61 billion, total deposits of $1.70 billion and total shareholders’ equity of $251.0 million.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
